subject: general
question: What changes take place in the guard cells that cause the opening of stomata?

options.text: Water enters the guard cells and they shrink
Water comes out of the guard cells and they shrink
Water enters the guard cells and they swell
Water comes out of the guard cells and they swell

solution:
The correct answer is __**Water enters the guard cells and they swell**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Water enters the guard cells and they swell** causing the stomata to open.
 
• Guard cells are specialized cells located in the epidermis of leaves, stems, and other organs that are used to control gas exchange.
 
• When water enters the guard cells, they become turgid and the stomatal pore opens.
 
• This mechanism allows for the uptake of carbon dioxide and the release of oxygen and water vapor during photosynthesis and respiration.
 
• Conversely, when guard cells lose water, they become flaccid and the stomatal pore closes, reducing water loss through transpiration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Guard cells** are the only epidermal cells that contain chloroplasts, which are essential for photosynthesis.
 
• The opening and closing of stomata are influenced by factors such as light, carbon dioxide concentration, and internal water balance.
 
• Stomatal movement is a critical process in plant physiology, impacting water use efficiency and photosynthetic capacity.
 
• Regulation of stomatal aperture is crucial for the plant's adaptation to environmental conditions.
 
• The process is also linked to the plant's internal circadian rhythms, which help optimize gas exchange and water use during different times of the day.
